g.text: C036a — Coupler-gap dependence and the exponential coupling fit (Figs 4.3-4.5)

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Wider gap → weaker coupling → longer cross-over length. One straight line on semi-log captures it all.

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Conditions: 500×220nm + 90nm slab · λ=1550nm · 20nm mesh · mode solver + EME

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: gap sets coupling exponentially (one straight line on semi-log); κ cycles as sin, so a narrow gap can still give ≈zero when the length completes a cycle.
